what_its_for: Midazolam is used to help you relax before a medical procedure or surgery, to help you sleep during certain medical tests, or to quickly stop severe seizures that last too long (called cluster seizures). It belongs to a group of medicines called benzodiazepines, which work by calming activity in your brain and nervous system.
how_to_take: Midazolam comes in different forms depending on how it is being used. In a hospital or clinic, a healthcare provider will give it to you as a shot into a vein or muscle. The nasal spray (Nayzilam) is sprayed into one nostril. The buccal or oral liquid form is squirted into the side of your cheek or swallowed. Always follow the exact instructions given to you by your doctor or the device instructions that come with your prescription. Never change the dose on your own.
dosing: Your dose depends on your age, weight, medical condition, and what the medicine is being used for. For seizure rescue sprays like Nayzilam, the usual adult dose is one spray (5 mg) into one nostril. If the seizure does not stop after 10 minutes, a second spray may be given into the other nostril. Do not use more than 2 sprays per seizure episode. Always follow your doctor's personalized dosing instructions exactly.
missed_dose: If midazolam is being used in a hospital setting, a nurse or doctor will manage your doses. If you are using the nasal spray at home for seizures, use it as soon as a prolonged seizure starts — do not wait. This medicine is only used when needed, not on a regular daily schedule, so a typical missed dose situation does not apply. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist right away.
storage: Store midazolam at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not freeze the nasal spray or liquid forms. Keep the nasal spray in its protective case when not in use. Keep all forms of this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while using midazolam — this combination can be very dangerous and may cause your breathing to slow down too much or stop. Avoid taking other sedatives, sleeping pills, opioid pain medicines, muscle relaxers, or anti-anxiety medicines unless your doctor approves, as they can all increase the risk of serious side effects. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert for at least 24 hours after receiving midazolam, or until you feel fully recovered. Avoid grapefruit juice, as it can affect how this medicine works in your body.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help right away if you or someone with you experiences: slow, shallow, or stopped breathing; severe drowsiness or you cannot be woken up; blue color on the lips or fingertips; a fast or irregular heartbeat; severe confusion or agitation; allergic reaction signs such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; or if the seizure does not stop after using the rescue nasal spray. If you use the nasal spray, always call 911 after using it for a rescue seizure, as directed by your doctor.
when_it_works: When given by a healthcare provider into a vein, midazolam usually starts working within 1 to 5 minutes. When given as a nasal spray, it typically starts working within 10 to 15 minutes. When given as a shot into a muscle, it may take 5 to 15 minutes. Effects generally last between 1 and 6 hours depending on the dose and how it was given.
special_populations: Children and elderly patients are more sensitive to midazolam and usually need lower doses. Elderly people are at higher risk for falls, confusion, and breathing problems. Pregnant women should avoid midazolam if possible, especially early in pregnancy and right before delivery, as it can affect the baby. Breastfeeding mothers should not breastfeed for at least 4 hours after receiving midazolam. People with liver disease, kidney disease, breathing problems such as sleep apnea, or heart problems should use this medicine with extra caution and close medical supervision.
